title: Pratap Singh v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunil Ambwani, J.; Aditya Nath Mittal, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; petitioner relegated to clause 6.5 and CGRF.
headnote: A consumer disputing a recovery citation and electricity bills, including post-disconnection minimum-guarantee charges, must first approach the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and thereafter the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum. A writ seeking to correct bills in the High Court without exhausting those statutory remedies under the Electricity Act, 2003 is dismissed.
facts: Pratap Singh ran a flour mill on an LMV-6 connection of 33 kVA, raised to 40 kVA on 4 December 2009. Supply was disconnected in November 2011 and the meter dismantled. A 26 February 2012 bill of Rs.4,24,985 (arrears and late-payment surcharge) was followed by a 19 March 2012 recovery citation for Rs.2,08,113 and other dues, including minimum-guarantee charges. He sought a writ quashing the citation and correcting the bills, alleging no post-disconnection consumption. He had made no representation to the department.

holding_units.holding: A consumer who disputes electricity bills, a recovery citation, and post-disconnection minimum-guarantee charges must first raise the grievance before the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and may thereafter approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum. A writ petition filed in the High Court to correct such bills without first exhausting those statutory remedies under the Electricity Act, 2003 is not maintainable and is dismissed.

not_decided.point: Whether the post-disconnection demand, including minimum-guarantee charges after the meter was dismantled, was justified
not_decided.note: Writ dismissed for non-exhaustion of clause 6.5 and CGRF remedies; merits of the bill and citation were not examined.
